title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Alyssa Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates the standard approach for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation across SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is to provide a single-source, reviewable, and repeatable process for producing high-quality, production-ready DevEx content that reduces developer onboarding time and lowers support volume.

Intended audience:
- Developer Experience engineers
- SDK maintainers
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers
- Technical writers

Scope:
- SDK reference & how-to guides (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go)
- Quickstarts and templates (starter apps and repos)
- API examples and canonical snippets for release notes and docs site
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, review, and rollback)
- Top support issues (triage, canonical fixes, and KB links)

Ownership and roles:
1. Author: DevEx engineer (creates initial draft).
2. Reviewers: SDK owner, Platform product manager, Technical writer.
3. Approver: DevEx lead for published content.
4. Maintainers: SDK owners (code snippets), Docs engineers (site templates).

Document structure (required for all DevEx pages):
- Title (concise): e.g. "Python SDK quickstart"
- Short intro (1-2 paragraphs): problem statement and expected outcome
- Prerequisites (versions, credentials, network requirements)
- Step-by-step quickstart or guide (numbered)
- Code examples (copy-paste ready) and minimal reproducible sample
- Troubleshooting and top support issues (links to KB)
- Ownership and maintenance notes (who updates when API changes)
- Related pages and changelog section

SDK Guides: standards and examples
- Languages supported: Python (>=3.9), Node (>=18), Go (>=1.20).
- Required sections per SDK guide: Installation, Authentication, Basic usage, Streaming, Function-calling patterns, Error handling, Pagination & batching examples, Advanced config and performance tips.
- Code snippet policy: keep snippets <= 40 lines, include explicit imports and client initialization. All snippets must be linted and runnable in CI snippet tests.

Example (Python minimal):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate(prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'")
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstarts and templates (starter repos):
- Template types: CLI demo, Web chat (React + backend), Embeddings indexer, Batch inference job.
- Each template repo must contain: README with features and run steps, Dockerfile, dev container (optional), CI workflow to run lint + snippet tests, LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.
- Quickstart checklist before merge:
  1. README includes TL;DR + 5 minute run instructions.
  2. Example secrets config and .env.example provided.
  3. GitHub Actions (or equivalent) to validate snippets and run unit smoke test.
  4. Link to the SDK guide and API reference.

API examples: canonical snippets and story patterns
- Organize examples by user story: "chat app", "document search + rerank", "real-time summarization", "mass embedding pipeline".
- For each pattern include: minimal code example, architecture diagram (ASCII or link to image), cost/latency notes, recommended model family and config (batch size, seq length).
- Example: streaming chat (Node):
```js
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY);
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-3b' });
stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk.text));
```

Docs site operating procedures (publishing lifecycle):
- Draft -> in_review -> published. Standard review window: 48 business hours.
- Required approvals: at least one SDK owner + one technical writer.
- CI gates: link-check, snippet-runner, spellcheck.
- Release cadence: evergreen docs are updated on major SDK releases (semver major/minor) or when breaking runtime changes are shipped.
- Emergency publish (security or urgent fix): follow the Emergency Docs Runbook: notify on #devex-docs, tag approver, ship change with a post-publish retrospective.

Publishing steps (numbered):
1. Create feature branch and add content under docs/ and snippets/.
2. Run local snippet tests: `scripts/run-snippet-tests.sh`.
3. Open PR with the "docs" template. Assign reviewers: SDK owner, tech writer.
4. After approvals, CI will run site build and snippet tests; fix any failures.
5. Merge during low-traffic window (preferred) and confirm on preview environment.
6. Update changelog entry: /docs/changelog/devex.

Rollback procedure (if site break occurs):
1. Revert the offending commit and push.
2. Notify #site-ops and #devex-docs.
3. Run a smoke test suite (login + 3 canonical snippets).
4. Postmortem required if outage > 30 minutes.

Top support issues & canonical fixes (maintained monthly)
- Issue: Auth errors: "401 / invalid API key"
  - Canonical fix: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set, show minimal cURL and SDK example, include common gotchas (trailing whitespace, env loading).
  - KB link: /kb/auth-invalid-api-key
- Issue: Streaming responses truncated
  - Canonical fix: Use the streaming client API and handle backpressure; ensure keepalive/timeout config on proxies (example nginx config provided).
  - KB link: /kb/streaming-truncation
- Issue: High latency on short prompts
  - Canonical fix: Pin to model variant with lower cold-start times (e.g. redwood-chat-1s) and enable prefix caching where appropriate. Provide config snippet for routing policy.
  - KB link: /kb/latency-short-prompts
- Issue: Incorrect embedding dimensions
  - Canonical fix: Verify model's embedding dimension (e.g. 1536 vs 3072) and ensure your downstream vector DB schema matches; provide migration snippet.
  - KB link: /kb/embedding-dims

Monitoring and metrics for docs quality:
- Track: PR-to-publish time, snippet-test pass rate, docs-related support tickets (by label), page view + time-on-page for quickstarts.
- Targets: keep PR-to-publish median <= 72 hours, snippet-test pass rate >= 98%, docs-related support tickets reduction of 25% year-over-year.

Maintenance cadence:
- Quarterly: full audit of quickstarts and templates, run snippet smoke tests, refresh README run instructions.
- Monthly: update Top Support Issues list and verify KB links.

Onboarding checklist for new DevEx contributors:
- Read this playbook and the docs site operating procedures.
- Run local snippet tests and preview environment build.
- Shadow an existing PR review and do one editorial fix PR.
- Take ownership of at least one quickstart template.

Appendix: useful CLI commands and CI snippets
- Run snippet tests locally:
  ./scripts/run-snippet-tests.sh --lang python --filter quickstart
- Build preview site locally:
  yarn workspace docs build:preview
- Example GitHub Actions job (snippet test):
  jobs:
    snippet-tests:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - run: ./scripts/run-snippet-tests.sh

Related pages:
- Developer Experience docs site operating procedures (link above).
- SDK repo READMEs (see related pages list).

Contact and escalation:
- Primary contact: @devex-team (Slack)
- Urgent site issues: ping #site-ops and assign an on-call docs engineer.
